transcript:
User: Make it quick, I'm on a job site. Forty-five seconds.
Agent: Got it, I’ll keep this super tight.  

So first—how’d you come across us: was it a voicemail from Jay, an ad, or were you just searching for help with missed calls?
User: Skip that. What's the cost and how does it stop me from missing 25 calls a week?
Agent: Totally get it, I’ll be fast.  

Most shops your size land around $400–$900/month, depending on call volume and hours; we’re usually cheaper than even a part‑time receptionist.  

We stop those 25 missed calls by answering every call on the first ring, grabbing name, number, what they need, and either booking them straight into your calendar or sending you a text/email summary so no lead slips.  

If we could turn even 5–10 of those 25 into actual booked jobs each week, is that worth a deeper 15‑minute call with Jay later today or tomorrow?
User: Fine, if it catches those calls it pays for itself. Book the demo. When?
Agent: Makes sense, that’s exactly how most folks look at it.  

We do a quick 20‑minute call with Jay, no commitment—are you better later today after 4, or tomorrow morning?
User: Tomorrow morning. 9 AM sharp. Eastern time. Lock it in. Done?
Agent: Got it, tomorrow at 9 AM Eastern with Jay for a 20‑minute no‑commitment walkthrough.  

Last thing—what’s your name so I can put it on the calendar and make sure Jay knows who he’s meeting with?
User: Boris Petrov. Petrov Landscaping. Faster next time, I have crews waiting. Is that all?
Agent: Thanks, Boris. You’re set for tomorrow at 9 AM Eastern with Jay to walk through how we stop those missed calls for Petrov Landscaping. That’s all from my side—if anything changes, you can just call this same number. Talk to you tomorrow!
